subject.title: Gateway restart drops queued and in-flight inbound messages

question: Should the canonical repair be the SQLite-backed followup queue persistence path from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572, a narrower drain-only mitigation, or a broader channel-level catch-up design?
rationale: Current OpenClaw policy rejects new runtime JSON sidecars for queue state, and there are multiple open partial PRs with different durability boundaries.

options.title: Use SQLite followup persistence
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 or a replacement as the canonical Phase 1 fix and keep this issue open until it lands.

options.title: Merge a drain-only mitigation
options.body: Prioritize flushing/deferred-drain behavior such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/46303 while leaving process-exit and downtime catch-up as follow-up work.

options.title: Redesign channel catch-up first
options.body: Pause the current PRs and define a broader provider ACK/history replay contract before changing core queue persistence.

recommendation.title: Use SQLite followup persistence
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 or a replacement as the canonical Phase 1 fix and keep this issue open until it lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The current strongest candidate implementation is the SQLite-backed durable followup queue PR authored by this person.
